nine_property_table.4_out_of_order_releases_only_owning: REPAIRED (dd787db on this branch; D47 is the merged implementation). The release was FIFO (popleft), not by the call that made it — two defects, both reproduced against a gated transport that holds the first request in flight until the test opens the gate. (a) The advisor's own out-of-order case: A ($0.06, 6000 tokens) in flight, B ($0.01) completes first — the old release took B's completion to mean A's reservation was gone, so reserved read $0.01 while A was still in flight, and when A then failed after dispatch the failure kept B's $0.01 as unreconciled liability, understating what the run may still owe by $0.05 (break-proof: '0.01 == 0.06'). Repaired: reserved keeps the in-flight call's $0.06 and the failure keeps A's own $0.06. (b) A blind call (unrated, no worst case) popped the rated call in flight beside it: reserved read $0.00 while $0.05 was held, and the ceiling, seeing $0.001 committed, admitted a second $0.05 call against a $0.08 ceiling while $0.10 was in fact committed (break-proof: '0.0 == 0.05'). POST-MERGE: the merged implementation is D47's (ruled and merged first, command 113's execution) — _Reservation carries (worst, function, model, released), release happens at the chat/rerank call sites (_release), _account books cost and releases nothing, and _fail_call keeps the failed call's own worst case behind the released flag. The property is identical; D47's tests (TestReservationsAreIdentifiedNotCounted, TestABlindCallReleasesNothing, TestAFailedCallBooksItsOwnWorstCase) supersede this command's TestReservationsAreOwnedByTheirCall and _GatedTransport, which the merge drops.

nine_property_table.9_every_terminal_reconciles: REPAIRED (33351ff). The API engine's exception terminal committed the row BLOCKED without ever assigning workflow.total_cost, so a run that paid for calls and then raised landed at total_cost 0.0, and no path recorded the client's unreconciled_liability anywhere on the API path (break-proof: the new test's 'total_cost == 0.002' read '0.0 == 0.002'). The worst case of a call that failed after dispatch is money that may still be owed — it is not spend, and it is counted against the ceiling for the rest of the run.
